newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower, lackluster cash prices.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower, lackluster cash prices.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended modestly lower in quiet trade, under pressure from a lackluster world cash market, CBOT pit traders said.
"The cash markets are just holding steady and not doing much," a pit trader said.
Traders focused on news that Cargill has applied for permission from the U.S. Treasury Department to sell grain to North Korea, and some of that grain could be rice.
"We know they need grain, but we don't know if it would be U.S. rice," said a pit trader.
Market dips met with scale-down buying, traders said.
Refco, LIT and Term Commodities were active traders of the January/March spread, sources said.
Rice futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 550 contracts, below the 939 contracts traded Friday.
Rice closed one to three cents per cwt lower, with January down three at $11.12 per cwt.
